text:
Friend, my lararium is empty:

since the hearth fire no longer burns,

our gods fled before the cold;

today tedium presides on their thrones

over the nuptials of silence and evening.


Destructive time does not pass in vain;

the courtyard eaves are in ruins;

the swallows no longer form there

their delicate house, with convex walls of mortar

and down for a tapestry.


What silence at the piano! Its moan

no longer vibrates in deserted spaces;

the nocturnes and scherzos have fled…

Poor cage without birds! Poor nest!

Mysterious coffin of dead trills!


Ah, if you could see your garden! No roses now,

nor lilies, nor silk-winged dragonflies,

nor fireflies of light, nor butterflies…

The rosebush branches tremble, frightened;

the wind blows, leaf litter rolls.


Friend, your mansion is deserted;

the black-green moss that adorns

the ruined lintels of the door

seems an inscription that says: Dead!

The north wind passes, and sighing: Weep!

translation.title: Friend, My Lararium Is Empty
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the domestic shrine, ruined garden, silent piano, and final inscription of mourning.
